title: The partnership with Harold Danko
summary: Danko's duos and quartets, Petrucciani heckling, and the Nice festival.

blocks.x: You’ve had two partnerships I just want to talk about briefly. One was you did a number of things with Harold Danko in the eighties: duo things, quartet things. Actually I even remember a gig the two of you were playing in the Village one night that Michel Petrucciani came and was heckling you.
Ooh. Wow, boy. He was a mean little guy sometimes.
Yeah. That was one of those nights.
But you did a lot of nice records with Harold and a number of gigs both here and in Europe right?
How did you feel about that relationship?

That was one of the few times I felt like I had some kind of a band and appreciated that. Being at Nice one year with Rufus and Al Harewood was kind of the last time that George Wein hired me after that for some reason. I thought “Gee, I finally got a band and it didn’t work out.” I remember we opened for Wayne Shorter and while Wayne’s band set up he was humming the first eight bars of Billy Bauer’s “Marionette” tune and things like that. Very friendly contour there . . . it didn’t impress whoever was advising George Wein.
